clinical.rationale: This secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective cohort suggests MRI alone is sufficient after abnormal XR or persistent pain, potentially reducing CT use in pediatric cervical spine clearance.

research.rationale: Leverages a large prospective multicenter trauma imaging cohort to answer a focused question about unnecessary dual cross-sectional imaging, with clear clinical follow-up.

papers.one_line: In children with abnormal cervical spine X-rays or persistent pain, CT added to MRI found no clinically significant injuries that MRI missed.

summary.why_it_matters: Children with abnormal cervical spine X-rays or persistent pain often get both CT and MRI; this analysis questions CT's added value.
summary.design: Secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective cohort of pediatric blunt cervical spine imaging at 72 US trauma centers.
summary.key_findings: Among 106 children with abnormal X-rays, 15.1% had CT-positive but MRI-negative findings, yet none were clinically significant or unstable. summary.bottom_line: When cross-sectional imaging is indicated, MRI alone is preferable when feasible; routine CT plus MRI is not supported. Outpatient reassessment with collar immobilization may be reasonable in selected neurologically intact children.
